title: What does it mean that a Stream does not store elements (pipeline over a source, lazy, pull-based)?
shortTitle: Why do streams not store elements?
keyPoints: A Stream is a pipeline description, not a data structure: it does not allocate memory to hold elements.
Execution is pull-based: the terminal operation pulls elements one at a time through the intermediate stages.
Stateless operations (filter, map) process one element at a time with O(1) memory.
Stateful operations (sorted, distinct) must buffer elements: sorted requires O(n) memory for the entire stream.
Loop fusion means multiple operations execute in a single pass per element, not separate passes per operation.
Short-circuit operations like findFirst and limit stop the pipeline early without processing all elements.
Infinite streams work because pull-based laziness means only the requested elements are ever generated.

s1_definition.oneliner: A Stream is a pipeline description over a source, not a data structure: it stores nothing, processes elements one at a time via pull-based lazy evaluation, and fuses multiple operations into a single pass.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Pipeline description**: calling `stream().filter().map()` builds a chain of operation descriptors like a recipe. No element is processed yet.
- **Pull-based**: the terminal operation drives execution by requesting elements one at a time from upstream.
- **One element in-flight**: for stateless operations (filter, map), only one element is being processed at any instant, requiring O(1) memory.
- **Loop fusion**: filter, map, and other stateless operations execute on the same element before the next element is pulled.
- **Short-circuit**: findFirst and limit stop the pipeline as soon as the result is determined.
- **Stateful exception**: sorted and distinct must buffer elements, requiring O(n) memory.
s1_definition.analogy: A Collection is like the National Bank of India vault with 10,000 cheques stored inside. A Stream is like the cheque-clearing conveyor belt: it stores zero cheques. Cheques enter from the vault (source), pass through verification (filter), get stamped (map), and reach the destination (terminal). The belt pulls one cheque at a time. If the destination says "I only need 5 cleared cheques" (limit/findFirst), the belt stops. The remaining 9,995 cheques are never pulled from the vault.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Pull-based execution (findFirst):
  ──────────────────────────────────
  findFirst: "give me ONE element"
       ↑
  map: "give me ONE element" → transforms → passes up
       ↑
  filter: "give me ONE element" → test → pass or drop
       ↑
  source: yields TXN-001 → filter drops
  source: yields TXN-002 → filter passes → map transforms
       → findFirst receives → STOPS!
  TXN-003 NEVER pulled!

  Loop Fusion (single pass per element):
  ──────────────────────────────────────
  Element 1: filter → map → collect  (one element through all stages)
  Element 2: filter → map → collect
  Element 3: filter → drop           (never reaches map or collect)
  NOT: filter-ALL → map-ALL → collect-ALL
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A Stream does not store elements. It is a pipeline description that processes elements on demand from a source. Execution is pull-based: the terminal operation drives the pipeline by requesting elements one at a time. Each element flows through all stateless stages before the next element is pulled, requiring O(1) memory.

This design enables three powerful capabilities. Loop fusion executes filter, map, and collect in a single pass per element, not three separate loops. Short-circuit operations like findFirst and limit stop the pipeline as soon as the result is determined. Infinite streams work because pull-based laziness means only requested elements are generated.

The exception is stateful operations like sorted and distinct, which must buffer elements internally. Sorted needs all elements before it can sort, requiring O(n) memory. Understanding stateless versus stateful helps order operations optimally: filter before sorted reduces the buffer size.

Remember one sentence: streams store nothing and pull elements one at a time, so filter-map-collect is one pass, not three.
